# The dataset

```
data/NP184_NP187_NP188_combined_DUAN_21-0/
  merged.curated.minimap2.bam       27.5 GB
  merged.curated.minimap2.bam.bai
```

Long-read single-nucleus RNA-seq of hiPSC-derived neurons from the Duan lab.
The same cells and donors as
[Liang et al., *Science* 392:eadw3949 (2026)](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.adw3949) —
this is a Nanopore assay on one of that study's libraries, and is not itself
published.

Numbers below are **measured from the BAM** unless tagged
*[metadata]* (from Table S1 of the paper, or `cell_barcodes_w_meta.txt.gz`)
or *[slides]* (the scNanoGPS statistics we were sent).

# Headline numbers

| | |
|---|---|
| Cell barcodes | **8,612** |
| Primary reads (= molecules) | **61,189,011** |
| Donors | **4** (2 male / 2 female, 2 SCZ case / 2 control) |
| Stimulation state | **0 hr only — unstimulated** |
| Cells with a donor assignment | 4,866 (56.5%) |

# Platform and processing

| | |
|---|---|
| Sequencing | Oxford Nanopore |
| Chemistry | 10x Genomics Multiome / scARC — 16 bp cell barcode + 12 bp UMI |
| Pre-processing | **scNanoGPS** *[slides]* |
| Aligner | minimap2, spliced mode |
| Reference | GRCh38, 10x `refdata-gex-GRCh38-2024-A` |
| Strandedness | `--strand reverse` |
| Annotation | IsoQuant v3.3.0 (`OUT.extended_annotation.gtf`) |

Two conventions inherited from scNanoGPS are worth knowing, because most
single-cell tooling assumes otherwise:

* the **cell barcode lives in the `RG` tag**, not `CB`
* the **UMI is appended to the read name** (`<ONT-UUID>_<12bp UMI>`), not in `UB`

Example read:

```
QNAME  281b9c59-a0da-477b-84b9-d9895f6ec585_TTCAAGATATAT
RG:Z:  TTCGTTAGTACCAGGT
```

# Cells

| | |
|---|---|
| Cell barcodes | **8,612** |
| — all exactly 16 bp, all carrying reads | |
| Median UMIs / cell | 4,967 |
| Mean UMIs / cell | 7,105 |
| Minimum | 508 reads / cell |

The 8,612 barcodes account for all 61,189,011 primary reads, so there are no
empty or orphaned read groups. The 508-read floor means empty droplets were
already filtered upstream.

This matches the scNanoGPS "Cell number" for group 21 / 0 hr exactly *[slides]*,
which is one of the strongest pieces of evidence for which library this is.

# Reads

| | |
|---|---|
| Alignment records | 85,465,939 |
| **Primary** | **61,189,011** |
| Secondary (multimappers, retained) | 23,879,762 |
| Supplementary | 397,166 |
| Mapped | 99.99% |
| Marked duplicates | 0 |

**Always filter with `-F 0x900`.** Secondary alignments are 28% of records and
inflate any naive count — unevenly, since they concentrate in repeats.

The BAM is already **UMI-deduplicated**: 1.01 reads per (barcode, UMI) pair,
so reads ≈ unique molecules.

# Read characteristics

| | |
|---|---|
| Median read length | **506 bp** (mean 617, p90 1,115, max ~6 kb) |
| Reads containing a splice junction | **27.3%** |
| Median per-read error rate | ~1.1% |
| Soft-clipped reads | 97.8% |
| **Reads with no base-quality string** | **20.5%** (`QUAL` = `*`) |

The near-universal soft clipping is untrimmed polyA/adapter. It turns out to be
harmless for isoLASER (its `large_soft_clip` filter removed only 225 of 585,767
reads).

The missing base qualities are more consequential than they look. Besides
mattering for variant calling, **mixed QUAL/no-QUAL reads silently break
`samtools fastq`**: it reported `processed 629035 reads` while writing only
14,255 — a 97.7% loss with no error. Splitting the input by QUAL presence
converts both halves correctly, so it is the interleaving that breaks it.
Convert with an explicit parser instead.

# Genomic context — mostly intronic

Read midpoints against the IsoQuant annotation, chr21:

| | Ours (chr21) | scNanoGPS, genome-wide *[slides]* |
|---|---|---|
| Exonic | 19.5% | 11.6% |
| **Intronic** | **74.2%** | **68.4%** |
| Intergenic | 6.3% | 20.0% |

**This is the single most important property for the splicing aims.** It is
single-*nucleus* RNA, so the library is dominated by unspliced nuclear
pre-mRNA. Reads sitting in introns cannot be assigned to a mature transcript,
which is exactly what exon-centric isoform methods require.

It directly explains the largest loss in the isoLASER pilot
(`unassigned_tx_id` = 53.8% of reads). That is inherent to the assay, not a
tunable parameter.

# Background to filter

* **rRNA carryover** — 677 k of chr21's 1.31 M primary reads lie in the
  chr21:8.2–8.6 Mb rDNA array. The rDNA scaffolds `GL000220.1` and
  `KI270733.1` are also heavily loaded.
* **Mitochondrial** — ~4.6% of reads overall, median 4.2% per cell.
* **Rat astrocytes** were in the coculture *[metadata]*. They are filtered out
  of the metadata file, but rat-derived reads may still be in the BAM.

## Assignment coverage

| | Cells |
|---|---|
| Barcodes in the BAM | 8,612 |
| With both a cell-line and a cell-type assignment | **4,866 (56.5%)** |
| Without an assignment in the mapping file | 3,746 |

The unassigned cells look lower quality — mean 8.2% mitochondrial versus 4.7%
for assigned cells — so they are largely cells that failed QC in the published
analysis.

The slides report **5,035** cells with a confident *cell line* *[slides]*. Ours
is lower because the mapping file we hold is restricted to cells also assigned
to GABA/nmglut/npglut, i.e. it is the intersection of the cell-line and
cell-type calls. For allele-specific splicing only the donor matters, so the
unfiltered cell-line list would be preferable.

## Sex verified independently

Scoring each cell on chrY-specific genes (PAR excluded) versus XIST gives
**47% male** among assigned cells, consistent with the 2M/2F design.

Worth recording as a cautionary note: before the donor labels arrived, the same
test on *all* 8,612 cells gave 65% male. The calls it made were 98% accurate,
but coverage was badly asymmetric — female cells went unassigned 55% of the
time versus 14% for male, because one XIST locus is a weaker detector than nine
pooled chrY genes. The method was sound; the marginal totals were not.

# Stimulation state — 0 hr only

The published design has three timepoints per batch (0 / 1 / 6 h after 53 mM
KCl), so batch 21 has libraries `21-0`, `21-1`, `21-6`. Matching our 8,612
barcodes against each:

| Library | Timepoint | Barcodes | Overlap with our BAM |
|---|---|---|---|
| **21-0** | **0 hr, unstimulated** | 5,592 | **4,866 — 87.0%** |
| 21-1 | 1 hr | 9,760 | 43 — 0.4% |
| 21-6 | 6 hr | 7,895 | 48 — 0.6% |

The 0.4–0.6% is what random 16-mer collisions between independent 10x libraries
would give. So **this BAM is the unstimulated library only**, and
`NP184`/`NP187`/`NP188` are most likely three sequencing runs of it rather than
three timepoints.

Corroborating evidence — immediate-early genes are low, with no activated
population:

| IEG | % of cells | IEG | % of cells |
|---|---|---|---|
| BDNF | 16.1 | NR4A1 | 2.8 |
| EGR1 | 12.6 | FOSB | 1.2 |
| FOS | 9.6 | ARC | 0.9 |
| JUNB | 9.6 | NPAS4 | 0.3 |

**The 1 hr and 6 hr Nanopore libraries do exist** *[slides]* — 12,023 and
10,051 cells respectively. We simply do not have them.

# What this means for the analysis

**Splicing changes during the neuronal response** cannot be done with this file:
there is no stimulated condition in it. It needs the `21-1` and `21-6` BAMs.

**Allele-specific splicing** is feasible now. We have four donors with direct
barcode-level assignment, so no genotype demultiplexing is required. The route
is: split the BAM per donor → run isoLASER per donor → `isolaser_joint` across
the four. See the [isoLASER page](isolaser.html).

Two caveats to size expectations:

* Four donors is a small cohort for anything genetic — the paper used 100 lines
  for its QTL mapping. What is realistically deliverable is allele-specific
  splicing within donors plus cross-donor consistency.
* Read retention through isoLASER is **14.8%** (measured on chr21), dominated by
  the intronic fraction above. And 97% of tested events were untestable for
  linkage, because a heterozygous SNP and the splicing event must fall on the
  same ~506 bp read.

# Open questions

1. Can we get the **1 hr and 6 hr** Nanopore BAMs?
2. Is there documentation for this BAM? It carries no sample-level annotation —
   `@RG` holds only a bare 16 bp barcode, with no `SM`/`LB`/`DS`.
3. Can we get the **cell-line assignment before the cell-type filter** (5,035
   rather than 4,866 cells)?
4. At what stage were the **base qualities lost** for 20% of reads?
5. Are there long-read data for **other coculture batches** beyond batch 21?
